An example of the analysis of incorrect miRNA RT and RT-PCR reagents. A) RT-PCR reagents for human miR-145-5p were obtained from the supplementary file of PMID: 25578496 , which included the stem-loop RT-primer and two RT-PCR primers for miR-145-5p labeled as a "forward" and "reverse" primer. B) The mature sequence of miR-145-5p was obtained by searching for "hsa-miR-145" in miRBase. Only the 5p sequence was analyzed as specified within the supplementary file (A). C) Manual comparison of the RT primer ( step 6.2 ) and the 3' end of hsa-miR-145-5p ( highlighted green ) revealed complementarity over at least 4 consecutive nucleotides. Manual comparison of the "reverse" RT-PCR primer did not show any sequence identity to the RT primer, and instead showed 100% sequence identity to the 5' end of hsa-miR-145-5p over 12 consecutive nucleotides ( highlighted blue ). Manual comparison of the "forward" RT-PCR primer ( highlighted grey ) showed no sequence identity to the RT primer or hsa-miR-145-5p. D) The " forward" RT-PCR primer sequence was used as a search query in Google Scholar. Search results revealed that this sequence is commonly used as a forward RT-PCR primer for BMI
E) A Blastn search using the parameters of step 5.2 confirmed that the "forward" RT-PCR primer sequence is likely to target BMI1 instead of hsa-miR-145-5p.

steps.title: Upload Publication to Seek & Blastn
steps.instruction: Upload the publication of interest in PDF format to the Seek & Blastn platform.

substeps.instruction: Click the Seek & Blastn link.
Select 'Browse' to upload the PDF file, then submit.
To upload multiple publications, compress the PDFs into a ZIP file and upload the ZIP file.

steps.title: Analyze Publication Results
steps.instruction: Wait for the analysis to complete and navigate to the output page.

substeps.instruction: Wait for the window to display the phrase 'All done: results_here'.
Click the hyperlink to open the Seek & Blastn output page.

steps.title: Review Tabular Output
steps.instruction: Examine the six-column output table to identify potential issues with the publication.

substeps.instruction: Check 'Tested file' column for links to the XML and PDF files.
Check 'Similarity' column for intertextual distance (OK: > 0.5; Close: 0.44-0.50; Very close: < 0.44).
Check 'Genes' column for gene identifiers and their frequency.
Check 'Cont. CL' column for cell lines associated with contamination/misidentification (ICLAC version 7.2).
Check 'Species' column for species identifiers; note that publications are considered human research if frequency of 'human' ≥ (most frequent 'not human' species - 1).
Check 'Sequences.html' column for Blastn results of extracted nucleotide sequences.

steps.title: Evaluate Sequence Flags and Claims
steps.instruction: Interpret the color-coding and integers associated with the extracted nucleotide sequences.

substeps.instruction: Identify error codes: -1 (unknown status), 0 (no error), 6 (targeting predicted non-targeting), 7 (non-targeting predicted targeting), 8 (targeting wrong gene/sequence).

Interpret hypertext colors: Green (claimed status agrees with verified status), Orange (low significance hits: ≥ 90% but < 100% identity over ≥ 15 nt within 3 nt of 3' end, or ≤ 100% identity over ≤ 16 nt), Red (conflicting status or no clear target), Grey (status undetected).
Verify text claims: 'Claims targeting', 'Claims non-targeting', or 'Undetected'.
Identify extraction errors: Sequences flagged as '(Seq. not correctly extracted (Char/long/ short)' must be manually copied from the publication.

steps.title: Manually Verify Flagged Sequences
steps.instruction: Perform manual validation for any sequence flagged with a red integer, orange/red/grey hypertext, or extraction error.

substeps.instruction: Visually inspect the publication to confirm if the sequence is claimed as targeting or non-targeting.
Run Blastn analysis for human sequences: Use 'Human genomic plus transcript (Human G+T)' database, 'somewhat similar sequences' optimization, and 'expect threshold' set to 1000.
If Blastn is inconclusive, use the UCSC Genome Browser (BLAT search): Genome: human, Assembly: GRCh38/hg38 (or as stated), Query type: BLAT's guess, Sort output: Query, score, Output type: Hyperlink.
If still inconclusive, run Blastn against the standard nucleotide collection (nr/nt) database, optimized for 'somewhat similar sequences', with 'expect threshold' set to 1000 to check other species.

steps.title: Verify miR RT-PCR Reagents
steps.instruction: Perform specialized validation for microRNA (miR) reagents.

substeps.instruction: For forward primers: Verify via Blastn or miRBase; accept if 3' end shows 100% identity to claimed miR over ≥ 12 consecutive ribonucleotides.

For RT primers: Retrieve miR sequence from miRBase (analyze both 5p and 3p if strand is not specified). Accept if RT primer shows ≥ 4 consecutive nucleotides of complementarity including the 3' end of the miR target.
For reverse RT-PCR primers: Compare to the RT primer (accept if 100% identity over ≥ 17 nt) or align 3' end to miR target (accept if ≥ 4 consecutive nucleotides are complementary).
If RT primer is unavailable and reverse primer is not complementary to miR target, search the sequence in Google Scholar to check if it is a known universal primer.

steps.title: Verify Flagged Cell Lines
steps.instruction: Investigate cell lines flagged in the 'Cont. CL' column.

substeps.instruction: Search for the flagged cell line on Cellosaurus.
Check the publication context to determine if the cell line is used appropriately or is an ambiguously named non-problematic line.

steps.title: Take Corrective Action
steps.instruction: If an incorrect nucleotide sequence or problematic cell line is confirmed, proceed with reporting.

substeps.instruction: Contact publishing journals, authors, or institutions.
Post comments on PubPeer (https://pubpeer.com/).
